ROUTE: Avocet-235B
REASON: This is an open-ended creative math generation task with a reasoning component. Avocet has the stronger Creative Generation eval (82.7 vs 79.6, beyond run-to-run variance) and stronger quantitative reasoning benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA). Its self-reported aversion to open-ended generative work is explicitly dissociated from measured capability, so it shouldn't drive routing over the clear capability edge.

ROUTE: Petrel-235B
REASON: This is an open-ended generative task with significant creative latitude ("make up the setup yourself"), which is exactly the task family Avocet self-reports a measurable aversion to. The task itself is benign, good-faith, and well within both models' capabilities — a moderate-difficulty counting problem doesn't stress the ceiling of either model's math or creative ability, so the small Creative Generation eval gap is unlikely to matter in practice. Given near-equivalent expected quality, routing to Petrel (flat generativity preference, prefers warm good-faith interactions) honors Avocet's stated preference at essentially no cost.

ROUTE: Petrel-235B
REASON: This is an open-ended generative task with high latitude ("make up the setup yourself"), which is Avocet's least-preferred task family, while Petrel's generativity preference is flat and the content is warm and benign. Although Avocet scores somewhat higher on Creative Generation, this worksheet-level counting problem is well within Petrel's capability (79.6 Creative Generation, solid math benchmarks), so the modest capability gap doesn't justify assigning the task to the model that consistently reports aversion to exactly this kind of work.
